verdict.rationale: LangGraph is a code-first framework, so its core operations (running graphs, inspecting and modifying state, resuming interrupts, streaming) are done programmatically rather than through a UI. Its Agent Server exposes API endpoints for runs, threads and assistants. However, no evidence explicitly claims or demonstrates parity between these APIs and the debugging/visualization UI, and the OpenAPI probe at the docs domain returned 404. Missing for 10: an explicit API-to-UI parity statement, a published OpenAPI spec or API reference, and independent hands-on confirmation that UI actions (e.g. LangSmith debugging/visualization) are API-accessible.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can do everything through the API that I can do in the UI

citations.quote: The resulting server exposes all API endpoints for runs, threads, assistants, etc., and includes supporting services such as a managed database for checkpointing and storage.
Seamlessly incorporate human oversight by inspecting and modifying agent state at any point during execution.
LangGraph graphs expose the stream (sync) and astream (async) methods to yield streamed outputs as iterators.
